subject: Demo Recap & Proposed POC Plan — FinServCorp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@finservcorp.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Demo Recap & Proposed POC Plan — FinServCorp

Hi Daniel / Alice,

Thanks for your time today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and a proposed PoC plan to validate Redwood Inference for the use cases we covered (real-time customer support summarization + high-volume embedding search).

Demo recap (high level):
- Showed low-latency chat generation with fallback routing to smaller model variants.
- Embedding pipeline: batch + incremental update pattern, 2–3ms per-embedding on our dedicated config in our benchmarks.
- Observability: token-level cost, per-route latency, and eval hooks.

Proposed PoC objectives / success criteria (suggested):
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 400ms for your 1–2k daily concurrent users.
2) Cost: per-conversation token cost <= $0.01 on average (target to be validated).
3) Quality: automated eval pass rate >= 85% on your provided prompt set (we'll run your 100 sample prompts).
4) Integrations: connectors for your S3 data export and Snowflake ingestion validated.

PoC plan (6–8 weeks recommended):
- Week 0: Kickoff, finalize success criteria & data access (owner: FinServ — Alice).
- Week 1–2: Provisioning & integration (Redwood infra + RBAC; owner: Redwood — Marissa + Neha).
- Week 3–5: Run evals, performance tuning (quantization profile, batching), iterate on prompts (owner: joint).
- Week 6: Final report & next-step decision (owner: FinServ exec sponsor).

Ownership / points of contact:
- FinServCorp: Alice Chen (technical lead), Daniel Wu (project sponsor)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, program owner), Neha Kapoor (Customer Success, technical coord)

Immediate next steps I suggest:
1) Review the attached detailed PoC plan (FinServ_POC_plan_v1.pdf) — it includes env requirements and a checklist.
2) Confirm the success criteria above or suggest edits by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-11).
3) If OK, propose a kickoff window the week of Nov 15 — we can reserve dedicated capacity for the first two weeks.

Attachments: [Attachment: FinServ_POC_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

Thanks again — happy to jump on a short follow-up to lock details.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — great demo and very clear plan. A few quick clarifications before we confirm:

1) Success criteria: For the quality eval, can you run the 100-sample prompt set against the "current-prod" model we use (we'll share) and against the Redwood config so we can compare regression/upgrade risk?
2) Security/compliance: procurement will need the SOC 2 Type II report and a short summary of data residency/retention controls — can you send those?
3) Timeline: Nov 15 kickoff works for the team, but procurement needs a formal scope-of-work (SOW) and an estimated spend range for the reserved capacity during the PoC.

Cc'ing procurement so they have visibility. Alice will coordinate the data access (S3 + sample prompts).

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Digital Ops | FinServCorp

Hi Daniel / Alice,

Thanks — great questions. Short answers and attachments below.

1) Comparative eval: Yes — please send the anonymized "current-prod" outputs or the prompt set and we'll run a side-by-side evaluation (we'll include the baseline in the final report). Suggested deliverable: accuracy/ROUGE-like metric + qualitative examples.

2) Security / SOC 2: Attaching a short security packet and SOC 2 summary. Public SOC 2 Type II report is available to customers under NDA; if procurement wants it we can start the NDA and share the full report. Short summary: data at rest encrypted (KMS), customer-configurable retention, audit logs for inference requests.

3) SOW / estimated spend: We can provide a draft SOW and a conservative spend estimate for the reserved capacity during weeks 1–2 (we'll include burst allowances). I'll loop in our finance/procure template if procurement needs it.

Proposed kickoff window: Nov 15–19. We can provision a dedicated pool that day to reduce warm-up variance.

I've uploaded the PoC plan and a one-page security packet here: https://drive.google.com/finserv-poc-plan (link) and attached the PDF (FinServ_POC_plan_v1.pdf).

Next steps (proposed):
- Alice: confirm data access & sample prompt set by 2026-11-11.
- Procurement: if OK, confirm NDA request and we will route the SOC2 under NDA.
- We: provide draft SOW and estimate by 2026-11-09.

Attachments: [Attachment: FinServ_POC_plan_v1.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

Best,
